claims.claim: Bloom Energy and Oracle expanded their partnership in April 2026 under a master agreement supporting up to 2.8 GW of fuel-cell capacity, with an initial 1.2 GW contracted and deploying.

factors.name: AI onsite-power demand
factors.basis: multi-gigawatt hyperscale commitment is direct evidence of demand for rapidly deployable onsite generation

risks.risk: Large hyperscaler programs increase customer concentration and manufacturing/deployment execution exposure.

causalEdges.mechanism: fuel cells can be deployed with data-center projects before equivalent grid expansion
causalEdges.falsifier: deployment delays or customers shift materially to alternative power architectures

unknowns.unknown: Full 2.8 GW is an agreement ceiling; only the initial 1.2 GW is described as contracted in the source.

claims.claim: Bloom reported 2025 revenue of $2.02 billion, up 37.3%, record full-year gross margin, 2.5x year-over-year product backlog growth, and a second consecutive year of positive operating cash flow.

factors.name: commercial execution
factors.basis: revenue, backlog, margin and operating-cash-flow progression support evidence of scaling execution

risks.risk: Backlog conversion and sustaining margins while scaling remain execution dependencies.

causalEdges.mechanism: onsite power orders convert into product deployments and service revenue
causalEdges.falsifier: backlog fails to convert or gross margins deteriorate materially

unknowns.unknown: No valuation conclusion is asserted from operating results alone.
